subject: Post-call: Private hosting qualification — residency, air-gap, network constraints
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@regtek-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — private hosting constraints and next actions

Hi Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and the asks we agreed to surface to make progress on a private/VPC-hosted deployment for RegTek: 

Pain points / regulatory drivers (as stated):
- Data residency requirement: patient data must remain within RegTek-controlled VPC in us-east-1; audit trail required for all inference requests.
- Regulatory air-gap: backups must be segregated to an offline storage facility for long-term retention (SLA: 7+ years).
- Strict outbound egress controls: only whitelisted IPs and destination FQDNs permitted; no arbitrary external telemetry.
- HSM/KMS requirement: customer-managed key material for model encryption and tokenization.

Technical constraints we noted:
- Limited NAT egress, most calls must be inbound-only via approved proxy.
- TLS termination happens at RegTek perimeter; Redwood must support mutual TLS to internal endpoints.
- Max burst RPS target for inference: 2500 requests/min with 99th perc latency goal of <120ms for single-turn text generation.

Agreed next steps (owners):
- Ben (Redwood) to validate network flows and provide a minimal inbound/outbound IP allowlist and port matrix — deliver by Oct 8.
- Karthik (Redwood Security) to draft KMS/HSM integration options and provide an initial security checklist (Doc attached).
- RegTek infra (Elena) to share an anonymized network diagram and egress policy in the Drive link so we can map proposed routes.

Attachments referenced: regtek-network-sketch.pdf (placeholder provided by RegTek during call), redwood-sow-draft.docx (initial SOW template).

I'll schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive next week to walk infra and security teams through the proposed architecture. Proposed slots: Oct 12 or Oct 13 (US ET). Please confirm availability.

Thanks again — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@regtek-health.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: RegTek Infra Team <infra@regtek-health.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — private hosting constraints and next actions

Vanessa — thank you for the summary, that matches up. A couple clarifications from my side: 

1) The offline backup requirement is strict: snapshots must be written to a write-once tape vault; activation requires two-person approval. Can you confirm Redwood has a pattern for write-once archival workflows?
2) We will need per-token logging for a 90-day window, but logs beyond 90 days must be redacted or moved to the offline vault.
3) On throughput — the 2500 RPS is a seasonal spike; our steady state is ~600 RPS. We need an autoscaling/burst pattern that prevents cold-start delays.

I attached the redacted network sketch (regtek-network-sketch.pdf). I can share a deeper topology once the NDA addendum is signed.

Elena
Elena Ruiz | Director, Infrastructure — RegTek Health

On Oct 6, 2026, at 13:02, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap...
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@regtek-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — private hosting constraints and next actions

Elena — good clarifications, thank you. Responses inline below and new asks: 

1) Write-once archival: Redwood supports a gated archival workflow — we can provide an export pipeline that pushes encrypted snapshots to your tape vault (customer KMS) and requires a two-person sign-off process. We'll need the vault's ingestion API spec or SFTP endpoint. (Karthik: please add required audit hooks and retention controls.)

2) Per-token logs: we can provide token-level telemetry for 90 days in the private control plane. After 90 days we can either redact or offload to the offline vault; we'll include both options in our SOW.

3) Autoscaling/burst pattern: the serving runtime supports continuous batching and warm pool of workers to reduce cold-starts. For the seasonal spikes we recommend a reserved-dedicated pool + short-term burst capacity. Ben will propose a sizing baseline and cost delta.

Ben, Karthik — owners for the following: 
- Ben: produce IP/port allowlist, recommended NAT/proxy patterns, and a baseline capacity plan for steady vs burst traffic. Target to share a one-page matrix by Oct 8 EOD.
- Karthik: provide HSM/KMS integration options, required attestations (SGX/TPM as requested), and a log-redaction pattern for >90-day retention. Target: Oct 9.

Elena — can you share preferred meeting time for Oct 12/13 (US ET)? We can lock in a deep-dive and invite your security and infra leads.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz

Attachment: redwood-sow-draft.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@regtek-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T07:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — private hosting constraints and next actions

Folks — quick status update from infra verification side.

- I ran the initial mapping against the regtek-network-sketch.pdf and sketched an allowlist: inbound TLS (443) via our customer connector, SSH only via jump-hosts (22), and outbound control-plane egress to the Redwoods management endpoints limited to three IPs (listed in the Drive link).
- I'll produce the one-page IP/port matrix and a recommended NAT/proxy pattern (to support mutual TLS) by Oct 8 EOD as promised.
- For autoscaling: my baseline suggestion is Reserved (2 nodes) + burst pool (scales to 6) with warm-cache retention to avoid cold starts. I'll include a cost delta and expected 99th latency numbers for that config.

I'll set up a short tech-deep-dive agenda and proposed diagram for Oct 12 11:00 ET (will adjust based on Elena availability).

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

We'll review Ben's matrix once posted. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Elena
